chunks: And that which Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a man who goes out for some need of his, while not intending travel, then continues in that and the going on keeps extending for him until it reaches eight farsakhs. How should he act regarding his salat? He said: He shortens, and he does not perform the salat in full until he returns to his home.

So the correct way of understanding it is that shortening becomes obligatory for him after he has covered eight farsakhs, until he returns to his home, because he has become a traveler even if he did not intend that at the outset. The first narration only indicated the obligation of performing in full during the period of his going the amount that we mentioned, and the two are not contradictory according to this interpretation.

key_terms.السَّفَرَ: travel that carries legal consequences for salat
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةَ فَرَاسِخَ: the travel distance that triggers the ruling of shortening salat
key_terms.مَنْزِلِهِ: his home, to which the travel ruling continues until return
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: he performs the salat in full
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: he performs the shortened form of salat

ai.seo_question: If someone did not intend travel at first but ended up going eight farsakhs, must he shorten his salat?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who did not initially intend travel, but whose movement gradually extends until he covers the legal travel distance. Once he has traversed eight farsakhs, he is treated as a traveler and must shorten his salat until he returns home.
